newsitem.title: SPAIN: Copper output to rise at Portugal Neves Corvo mine.
newsitem.headline: Copper output to rise at Portugal Neves Corvo mine.

text.p: The mining rate at the Neves Corvo mine in Portugal has been increasing regularly since the operation's early years, and higher copper and tin production is expected this year, Jose Morales, President of Minas de Almagrera SA, said on Wednesday.
"A mining rate of 1.5 million tonnes was achieved in the early years of the mine and this has been regularly increased," Morales said at Metal Bulletin's International Copper Conference.
In 1996, 1.9 million tonnes of ore were mined and treated and the objective for 1997 is 2.1 million tonnes, he said.
The ore is treated at two concentrators at Neves Corvo -- the copper plant, which treated 1.49 million tonnes of ore in 1996, and the tin plant where throughput was 0.47 million tonnes.

Morales estimated that copper production this year at Neves Corvo would rise to 116,533 tonnes, up from 1996's 107,617 tonnes, but down from the 1994 level of 130,245 tonnes due to falling ore grades.
The strategy was to increase ore output in order to offset the drop in grades, he added.
Looking at the new open pit mine at Los Frailes in Spain, Morales said copper production would increase from 3,600 tonnes in 1997 to 6,900 tonnes by 2001.

Output of other metals would be higher, with zinc production climbing from 76,800 tonnes to 125,000 tonnes. Lead output was estimated increasing from 29,500 tonnes to 46,000 tonnes during the same time-span.
